General Building (B)

The B exam leans residential and wood-frame: framing, seismic hardware, stucco and finishes are over 40% together. Contractors who mostly build steel and industrial work should study these closely.

SectionTopicKey point
PlanningConcrete volumeL × W × T (ft) ÷ 27 = cubic yards; order 5–10% extra
PlanningRoofing square1 square = 100 sq ft
PlanningRebar size#n = n/8 inch; #4 = ½ inch
Core tradesConcreteDesign strength at 28 days; slump measures workability; 3 in cover against earth
Core tradesElectrical14 AWG for 15 A, 12 AWG for 20 A; GFCI in baths, kitchen counters, garages, outdoors
Core tradesPlumbing¼ in per ft slope for drains 3 in and smaller; vents protect trap seals; two seismic straps on water heaters
FramingAnchor bolts½ in, ≤ 6 ft apart, within 12 in of plate ends; treated sill plates on concrete
FramingTop platesDoubled, joints offset ≥ 24 in
FramingStairs and guardsRiser ≤ 7¾ in, tread ≥ 10 in; guards 36 in residential, 42 in commercial
FramingStuccoScratch → brown → finish
Finish tradesGypsum boardType X fire-rated; MR moisture-resistant
Finish tradesEgress windows5.7 sq ft net (5.0 at grade floor); sill ≤ 44 in
Finish tradesCeilings and alarmsHabitable rooms ≥ 7 ft; smoke alarms in bedrooms, outside sleeping areas, every story
SafetyLadders and trafficExtension ladders 3 ft above landing; flaggers use STOP/SLOW paddles

References: CSLB Law & Business study guide · CSLB General Building study guide · CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book.
